caption:
Amazon is hiring for a "new-to-world robot product" meant to work alongside families at home, according to job listings CNBC found.
The biggest clue is Sprout, a 3.5 foot humanoid from Fauna Robotics, the startup Amazon bought in March.
Amazon's last home robot, Astro, reached only a few thousand customers.

Would you let a humanoid robot live in your house?

paragraphs.text: Amazon is assembling a team to build a new robot for the home, according to job listings and LinkedIn profiles reviewed by CNBC in a report published on November 8, 2026. The company has created a Personal Robotics Group and is recruiting for what its postings call a "new-to-world robot product."

One engineering listing, since taken down, described a robot able to move through changing home environments and operate on its own alongside family members. Android Headlines reported that a June posting said the goal is robots that are "not just functional, but delightful."

The postings cover more than research. An October listing seeks a field support engineer to handle customer support and repairs in person, a role that suggests plans for a device that ends up in customers' homes. Another posting asks for a designer to define what it feels like to live with a Fauna robot.

Amazon has not shared a design, a price or a release date. According to Android Headlines, much of the team that worked on Amazon's earlier Astro robot has moved to the new project, and Amazon has also hired a roboticist from MIT.

The clearest clue is Sprout, a humanoid built by Fauna Robotics. Amazon bought Fauna in March 2026. The New York startup was founded in 2024 by former Meta and Google engineers, and roughly 50 of its employees joined Amazon in the deal, Android Headlines reported. Fauna now operates as part of the Personal Robotics Group.

Fauna began shipping Sprout in January 2026 as a platform for researchers, educators and commercial developers. The company lists it at 1.07 meters, about 3.5 feet, and 22.7 kilograms, about 50 pounds, with 29 degrees of freedom and an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin computer. Android Headlines reported that it sells to developers for $50,000 and was designed to be safe enough to stand next to a child without a safety cage.

Amazon has tried this category before. It unveiled Astro in 2021 at $1,450. The wheeled robot could roam a house, recognize faces and act as a mobile security camera, but it stayed invite only and reached only a few thousand customers before Amazon wound it down in 2024, according to TipRanks and Android Headlines.

Amazon shares rose in premarket trading on November 9 after the reports, TipRanks said. The site noted that Chief Executive Andy Jassy's most recent shareholder letter describes AI and robotics as among the biggest inflections of our lifetime, and that rivals including Tesla with Optimus and 1X with its Neo humanoid are also aiming robots at household chores.

A small two-legged humanoid is a different bet from Astro, a wheeled robot that largely served as a mobile security camera. Hiring for in-home repair staff and for a designer focused on daily life with the robot suggests Amazon is thinking about a consumer product rather than another lab project, although the company has confirmed none of these plans.

The next signal to watch is whether Amazon shows Sprout or a new robot at a device event, and whether it names a price that families could realistically pay after Astro's $1,450 tag failed to find a wide audience.
